paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Next slide. This is an yi-dak [YI DAGS] — a hungry ghost. This one is too cute — I love this one. It's kind of cute, but it's not a cute rebirth at all. Another word for it is a craving spirit. It wants things but really can't get them.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Next slide — dundro [DUD 'GRO], animals. It looks super cute, right? They're doing that thing where everyone's looking at the camera and having a good time. We think being an animal is all cute. But it's a particular kind of suffering — constantly being afraid of being eaten.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Next slide. This one is called humans — all the different kinds of humans. Being a human also has some very specific kinds of suffering, which our course will get into. But the human is in a perfect balance — there's enough suffering that you're motivated, but enough goodness that it doesn't hurt too much. There's a balance between good and bad. Because we know that when things are good, you're only waiting for the next tragedy to come — you know it's going to come. But if you're able to strike a good balance and use it, it can propel you to that really narrow band of great meditation that Ray talked about. Animals can't get there. But anything above a human can't get there either. We'll talk about that.
